author: xdestron
quote: Despite thirteen years of hype and undeniably impressive graphics, Grand Theft Auto VI ultimately buckles under the weight of its own obsession with hyper-realism. In trying to replicate the grounded, slow-burn simulation of Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar stripped away the immediate, anarchic sandbox fun that defined the franchise, replacing it with tedious chores, sluggish pacing, and restrictive inventory mechanics that make simply causing chaos feel like a hassle. The narrative struggles to justify the glacial opening hours, leaving Jason and Lucia's Bonnie-and-Clyde dynamic feeling surprisingly flat alongside dated, rigid mission design that punishes creativity. Paired with a jarring 30fps cap on consoles and no PC release in sight, Vice City ends up feeling less like a thrilling criminal playground and more like a gorgeous, overly serious tech demo that forgot how to be fun

author: xdestron
quote: Nintendo COOKED, and they used the perfect amount of seasoning. The game is beautiful, and the added context around character interactions only makes the story more enjoyable and impactful. The soundtrack is still the GOAT.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: xdestron
quote:
Is it hard? Yes
Is it maybe the best Metroidvania ever made? Also yes

This game is an indie masterpiece the likes of which no AAA company could even dream of making. It's the kind of game made by passionate developers who know exactly what kind of game they want to make. 

The world and level design are peak. The bosses are varied in both mechanics and challenge. The music is great. The gameplay and controls are best in class. The story is great, once again told in-game through interactions with the world and a few choice cutscenes. It ties into Hollow Knight in a satisfying way.

All in all, it's hard to find faults with this game. There was so much more content than I was expecting. The game world just kept opening up, and changing in interesting ways. Yes, there are frustrating parts and questionable design decisions, but I can't take off points from this masterpiece because of that.

author: xdestron
quote:
No. It's not a masterpiece. This game was overrated by people who were enthralled by the first 2 acts. 
Unfortunately, the Act 3 twist totally ruins the entire game. Horrible, lazy writing that invalidates almost everything that happened before. FFX did the same twist, only a million times better, in a way that didn't ruin the rest of the game.
Sure, the gameplay is good. It's a fun game. But man did they botch the story. The ceiling of this game is an 8 because of it.

author: xdestron
quote: You have to try to botch a game (and game studio) this hard. The game had a lot of potential but it's clear that DEI and ESG investment dollars were the first priority when making this game. Do not buy this game. Let publishers know we want real videogames from real passionate developers again.

author: xdestron
quote:
It's one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. Between the graphics and the sound design, this is the first game I played that feels "next-gen". It's also just a good Souls game. 

I like the level design, and I like the bosses. The only thing that brings it down for me is the "cheapness". I have played most of the Souls games and this one has the most parts that feel like unfair traps. I might have to do a second runthrough now that I know the layout, maybe my opinion will change. But until then, it sits as the best looking Souls games and one of the most fun.

author: xdestron
quote:
Boring! That's all I can say about this game. It starts off boring, and it never really gets any better.
It's simply built around the addiction of getting new items, which doesn't happen nearly often enough. It's clearly built for whales and people who love to grind.

I can't even bring myself to finish the campaign because, well, it's just not fun!  Another game where video game urinalists are totally out of touch!

author: xdestron
quote:
In order to appeal to the casual audience, Square-Enix has abandoned everything that made the FF franchise great. This is not a JRPG, it's barely even an RPG. It's more like Devil May Cry: Final Fantasy Edition.
If you want party management, exploration, turn-based combat, etc., I recommend Octopath Traveler 2. If you want bombastic QTE button-mashing boss battles, I guess that's what Final Fantasy is now.

author: xdestron
quote:
This game is so much more than just nostalgia bait, it's the tightest, most fun, side-scrolling brawler on the market. The gameplay and fighting systems are legitimately perfect. The Mr. X DLC adds so much replayability to the game it's incredible. I wasn't sold on the soundtrack at first, but over time I came to really like it.

It's just a total package, especially if you're a fan of the series. It stays true to it's classic roots as well!

author: xdestron
quote:
Incredible improvement on the original. Capcom has been killing it with RE and this game is no exception.

Great story, great gameplay, memorable villains and boss fights, what more can you ask?

author: xdestron
quote: Caused me to finally "get" the Dark Souls formula. I've since beaten DS1, DS3, this game 3 times, and Demon's Souls up next. The build variety and combat in this game are simply unmatched. I can barely stand the mashy combat style of games like GoW or Spider-man anymore.

author: xdestron
quote:
Very samey compared to the first game, except weaker story and pacing. I was very disappointed that the upgrade trees were practically identical.

Kratos felt neutered in this game, while the spotlight shifts towards Atreus. Honestly, the Kratos of the original trilogy feels completely gone now. He speaks more of friendship and against war than I ever cared to hear Kratos speak.

The story was unbearably slow in parts (mostly Atreus parts) while the characterization of certain gods felt strange. It was more boring than a GoW game should be. It even felt like more of a walking simulator than the first game. Room -> fight -> squeeze thru a crack in the wall -> walking while talking -> another crack -> another fight. Rinse and repeat.

I would have appreciated some more innovation to make this feel like more of a sequel instead of an expansion. It's the same game but worse.

author: xdestron
quote:
Anyone referring to this as a remake needs to research the difference between remake and remaster.
This is the second remaster of this game. Repackaged for $70.
Naughty Dog is trash and has no originality left in the tank.
game_title: The Last of Us Part I

author: xdestron
quote:
This game was way better than I was expecting. I was never a huge fan of the Metroid series, even though I did really like indie titles like Hollow Knight, but I think this game just made me a fan.

The entire game is extremely polished. The environments, the animations, the little touches, they're all there to the point  where you could tell the developers really cared about making this game great, which they did. I feel like I should really emphasize the art style and the environments because they really pop and look incredible everywhere you go.

The gameplay is great. The abilities come at a nice clip, and there are a lot of them. And they do a great job of making you feel more powerful as you go. Combat is fun, and the bosses battles are amazing and fun. Yes they are hard. Yes you will die a lot. The great part about this game is that it lets you retry immediately. It's almost like a roguelike at times where you get better at a part by replaying it over and over. A boss or EMMI encounter that seems impossible at first suddenly becomes easy. It's definitely empowering. I never found the difficulty to be too much (I'm near endgame)

The only other thing I'd like to point out in closing is that Samus is totally badass in this game.

10/10 must play if you own a Switch.

author: xdestron
quote:
This sequel was butchered by Naughty Dog like Ellie taking a knife to the throat an innocent NPC.
This is probably the worst sequel I've ever played. It's actually nothing like the first game outside of gameplay (which is EXACTLY THE SAME). The themes and tropes of the first game have been replaced with "muh cycle of revenge". The entire message of the game is not subtle, but rather beaten into your head over and over, similar to the fate of a beloved main character.
The story is actually one of the most pretentious dog piles I've ever witnessed. The writing thinks it's 100 times more profound than it actually is. In reality it's about as deep as a puddle.
The entire game exists to massage the egos of the developers.
Naughty Dog no longer gets a pass after this one.
game_title: The Last of Us Part II

author: xdestron
quote: This game franchise is like the Transformers of videogames. They think by adding cliche plot twists and explosions the game is somehow better. In reality, it's the same rehashed garbage that gets more stale and less fun at each iteration. Not only that, but the player base consists of the lowest common denominator of humanity. It really tells you a lot about the game. I'll never understand why this garbage gets hyped so much.
